name: State Machine Replication
description: Foundational paradigm for building fault-tolerant services by executing the same sequence of deterministic commands on multiple replica nodes. Ensures consistency across distributed systems even when individual nodes experience failures.
common_pitfalls: Assuming non-deterministic operations will naturally converge without coordination.

name: Distributed Consensus Foundations
description: Core theoretical principles required for multiple independent processes to agree on a single data value or execution path. Encompasses models of partial synchrony and crash-fault tolerance (CFT).
common_pitfalls: Confusing consensus safety properties with liveness guarantees.

name: Paxos Protocol
description: The classic family of protocols for solving consensus in a network of unreliable processors. Establishes distributed agreement through proposer, acceptor, and learner roles utilizing ballot numbers.
common_pitfalls: Overlooking the complexity of multi-Paxos implementations for log replication.

name: Raft Leader Election
description: The foundational mechanism in Raft where nodes transition between follower, candidate, and leader states. Utilizes randomized timeouts to prevent split votes and ensure timely cluster management.
common_pitfalls: Assuming multiple leaders cannot emerge if network partitions occur improperly.

name: Raft Log Replication
description: Process by which the designated leader accepts client commands, appends them to its log, and forces followers to mirror the entries. Guarantees that consistent log prefixes imply identical state machine execution.
common_pitfalls: Failing to handle lagging follower logs correctly during network reconvergences.

name: Log Invariants & Safety Proofs
description: Mathematical guarantees ensuring that once a log entry is committed, it will persist across all future leaders. Enforces properties such as Leader Completeness and State Machine Safety.
common_pitfalls: Assuming uncommitted entries from past terms are automatically safe to overwrite without constraints.
